newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates steady in week.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates steady in week.

text.p: Average commitment rates on U.S. 30-year fixed rate mortgages were unchanged at 7.84 percent in the week ending March 14 while 15-year rates fell to 7.34 percent from 7.35 percent the prior week, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
But one-year adjustable-rate mortgages inched upward to 5.61 percent from 5.54 percent last week, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year loan rate averaged 7.83 percent, the 15-year 7.32 percent and the ARM 5.55 percent.

"Since (Federal Reserve) Chairman (Alan) Greenspan's remarks pushed interest rates up two weeks ago, the economic news continues to point to a strong economy with no great threat of inflation," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"With these conditions in place, interest rates remain steady this week. Further, it appears these figures will stay stable through the coming week, at least," Van Order added.
In its Beige Book issued Wednesday, the Federal Reserve said although U.S. job markets are tight, wage gains appear moderate and price pressures temperate.
Last week the Labor Department reported a U.S. February unemployment rate of 5.3 percent. On Friday the department will issue February producer prices.
Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.4 percent on the ARM, also unchanged from the prior week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
